Wedgewood Partners, an investment management company, released its third-quarter 2026 investor letter. The letter can be downloaded here. Wedgewood Composite delivered a net return of 2.5% in the quarter, compared to 2.3% for the Standard & Poor's 500 Index, 0.9% for the Russell 1000 Growth Index, and 2.6% for the Russell 1000 Value Index. Surging Treasury yields and macro headwinds have heavily pressured rate-sensitive stocks and market breadth, driving equal-weighted S&P 500 underperformance. However, AI resilience and mega-cap tech pushed the NASDAQ 100 to record highs. While rising inflation, energy price spikes, and higher interest rates continue to pressure broader equities, the firm is actively deploying capital into compelling new positions, recently adding Toll Brothers, Hermès, and TJX Companies. Also, check the strategy's top five holdings to see its best picks in 2026.

In its Q3 2026 investor letter, Wedgewood Partners highlighted Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) as a standout performer this quarter. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META), the parent company of dominant social media platforms, is a multinational technology company that develops products to connect people. On October 15, 2026, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) closed at $736.72 per share with a $1.88 trillion market capitalization. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) posted an 11.61% YTD gain, trading within a 52-week range of $520.26 to $779.82.

Wedgewood Partners stated the following regarding Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) was another standout performer in the portfolio this quarter. Revenues grew 28%, and the Company launched a slew of AI products and updates that the market viewed positively. Meta has a long history of launching massive, objectively successful products. Yet the market often ignores them or even penalizes them. While Meta's Metaverse investments are a clear reason to be skeptical that management will bat 1.000, they are hardly a reason to discount every clear and obvious home run, or even grand slam. More recently, the Company's Threads app, launched just 3 years ago, has over 500 million monthly active users. This quarter, Meta also rolled out its Muse Agent, which users can set on autopilot to handle mundane but productive tasks like lowering phone bills or renewing license plate tags. The Muse Agent works in tandem with a private virtual machine (we estimate its value at $500 to $1,000) that every user gets for free and that maintains the user's privacy and security throughout the process.

While it is still early days, the Company's advancements on the LLM frontier, along with its long history of working with encryption, especially through WhatsApp, have made the rollout and execution of Muse Agent among the best since OpenAI launched ChatGPT. Over the next several years, we think Meta has plenty more AI products and investments that will generate returns on par with those of past years."

title: Meta launches new ‘open’ AI model – and it comes with a big surprise
detail:
Meta launches new ‘open’ AI model – and it comes with a big surprise
Andrew Griffin
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:27 AM MST 3 min read
META
AAPL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
(Reuters)

Meta has launched a powerful new "open" model, which contains at least one surprise.

The company says that the system, named Meta Spark Open, is the most powerful open weight model made by a US company. Open weight models are so-called because their developers make public the "weights" that decide how a system will respond to a request.

That means that they are available for anyone to download to their own devices, as well as to adjust. It means that they can be used on a device itself, rather than on a company's servers, as well as allowing them to be adapted to different purposes.

It was that particular characteristic that led to a surprise perhaps even bigger than Meta's announcement.

As Meta announced the new model, it also said that it had been working with Apple to ensure that it ran well on its Mac Studio computer. Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg wrote in a post on X that Muse Spark Open "runs great" on Apple's hardware, because of work with Apple and its new chief executive, John Ternus.

"Congrats to the team!" Mr Ternus wrote in reply. "Amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open's caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk."

The collaboration represents an unexpected peace among the two companies, which have long had a complicated and sometimes antagonistic relationship. The two have repeatedly clashed over a variety of issues, most notably conflicts between Apple's commitment to privacy and Meta's use of advertising in its business model.

But the release of the new system seemingly shows how the race to build and embrace AI features is bringing unexpected collaborators together. It also demonstrates how some in the technology industry including Apple and Meta are looking to move beyond AI systems that rely on controversial data centres and difficult-to-acquire chips, and instead move towards running artificial intelligence on people's own devices.

That is made more possible with the release of open weight models, since they can be downloaded and installed on users' own computers. Meta's release of Muse Spark Open follows the launch of a number of open weight models in recent days, including from competitors such as Nvidia and Mistral.

Despite the positives of open weight models, however, many US companies including Meta have chosen to release most or all of their systems in ways that ensure they control the whole experience. They have argued that doing so keeps the models safer because the companies can more effectively ensure they are not used for dangerous purposes, but it also means that they can increase revenue by requiring customers to pay for monthly subscriptions or show advertising.

Investing.com -- RBC Capital Markets raised its price target on Shopify to $200 from $180, citing strong growth momentum and the potential for the e-commerce platform to exceed market expectations for third-quarter results and fourth-quarter guidance.

The revised target reflects confidence in Shopify's ability to sustain growth above 30%, supported by resilient merchant sales, pricing increases and opportunities to expand its role in AI-driven commerce.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Shopify has been pushing to position its commerce infrastructure at the centre of AI-powered shopping. Earlier this week, the company expanded access to its product catalogue to more AI agents, allowing shoppers to discover and purchase products through assistants connected to its Shop app. The move builds on its partnership with Meta's Muse and its Shop Pay checkout technology.

RBC expects Shopify's recent price increases to add 110 basis points to its annualized growth rate, further supporting its expansion. The bank maintained its Outperform rating, citing the potential for the company's valuation to rise as investors recognize its sustained growth and AI opportunities.

Shopify is scheduled to report its third-quarter results on November 3. The company reported 34% revenue growth in the second quarter and forecast low-thirties percentage revenue growth for the third quarter.
